findings.title: Strategy close() shuts down the shared FixedQueuePool, which the factory reuses across rebalances
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() (and terminate()) call self.queue_pool.shutdown(). The FixedQueuePool is created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and passed to every strategy returned by create_thread_queue_parallel_worker. Arroyo creates a new strategy on each partition assignment and closes the old one on rebalance. After the first close, all worker threads exit and the queues are shut down, but the factory still holds the same pool. Any later strategy then calls queue.put() on a shut-down queue, which raises queue.ShutDown. submit() catches that and logs it, so messages are silently dropped and their offsets are marked complete, and the commit thread keeps running against a dead pool. The pool should be owned by the factory (shut down only in factory.shutdown()), or each strategy should own its own pool.

findings.title: queue.ShutDown only exists on Python 3.13+
findings.body: queue.ShutDown is referenced in the except clauses of OrderedQueueWorker.run (lines 132 and 142) and in the queue.shutdown() call path. On Python versions before 3.13 the module has no ShutDown attribute. The except expression is evaluated only when an exception is raised, so the worker thread would die with AttributeError as soon as get() or the processing block raises, instead of shutting down cleanly. The repo's supported Python version must be checked, or a sentinel-based shutdown should be used.

findings.title: Queues are unbounded, so the claimed backpressure does not exist
findings.body: The class docstring of SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy promises 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', but queue.Queue() is created with no maxsize (line 185) and submit() never raises MessageRejected. If the broker delivers faster than the workers process, items accumulate in memory without bound and the consumer never pauses. Either set a maxsize and reject messages when full, or remove the claim.

findings.title: Offset gaps stop commits permanently and the scan is O(range)
findings.body: get_committable_offsets iterates every integer from start to max_offset and breaks at the first integer that is not in all_offsets (lines 89-93). Kafka offsets are not always contiguous (compacted topics, transaction markers, deleted records). If an offset never appears, the highest committable offset stays stuck at the gap. Committed progress then stops for the life of the process, lag grows, and after a restart the same range is reprocessed. The loop is also proportional to the offset span rather than the number of tracked offsets, so one long-outstanding offset with large offset jumps makes every commit tick (under the partition lock) iterate a huge range.

findings.title: commit_function is called from the commit thread, not the Arroyo processing thread
findings.body: _commit_loop runs in its own thread and calls self.commit_function(committable), which invokes the Arroyo Commit callable. Arroyo's commit is normally invoked from the strategy's processing thread, and the KafkaConsumer is not documented as thread-safe. Calling it concurrently with the poll loop can corrupt consumer state or raise errors. The commit should be marshalled back to the main thread, for example in poll().

findings.title: Error-handling test asserts the opposite of its stated behaviour
findings.body: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling says errors 'don't block offset commits for other messages', but its final assertion is `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`, which requires that nothing is committed. Since the failing message is swallowed and offset 101 completes, the implementation commits 102 and this assertion would fail if the test ran to completion. The loop may also exit early, so the test can pass without verifying commit behaviour. The assertion should check that the partition is committed past the failed offset.

findings.title: shutdown() cannot release a pool that a strategy has already shut down
findings.body: Because strategies also shut the pool down on close (see queue_consumer.py close()), the factory's shutdown() path and the strategy path both call FixedQueuePool.shutdown() on the same object. The second call is harmless only because shutdown is idempotent in practice. Ownership of the pool should be clarified so that exactly one component shuts it down.

findings.title: Kafka integration test swallows cleanup errors and uses private StreamProcessor methods
findings.body: The finally block wraps admin_client.delete_topics in `except Exception: pass`, hiding failures that would leave test topics behind. The test also calls the private processor._run_once() and processor._shutdown(), which are not a stable API. The test is tied to internal Arroyo details and can break on unrelated library updates.
